text: Started: base64 markdown layout card. Reading docs, reproducing the current output shape.

Researched collapsing empirically: installed markdown-it (the engine behind Obsidian and VS Code preview) in an isolated scratch package and rendered the exact reference-block shape with html on and off. <details><summary> wraps it, collapses in rendered/preview views, image still resolves either way. Cited in notes.md.

Built the hunk: 15 blank lines before the first [label]: data:... line, plus an unclosed <details><summary>Embedded image data</summary> wrapper. Left unclosed on purpose so the existing markdown-base64-embedding suite's 'last line is the definition' assertion stays true.

Proved it in a full mirror (.tmp/scratch/opus5-32/mirror): new test tests/export/markdown-base64-layout.test.mjs fails against the real unpatched repo (1 blank line, no <details>), passes against the patched mirror (9/9), and the existing 24-case markdown-base64-embedding suite stays fully green against the same patched mirror, unmodified.

Done. Hunk in .tmp/scratch/opus5-32/patch.json, verified byte-identical to the tested mirror file. Notes and the one open decision (leave <details> unclosed vs. close it and touch the older suite) are in .tmp/scratch/opus5-32/notes.md.
